rationale: Source work to ground the active Candidate 0069a1fe5be04660b3b91f31ac2394d4 (the Accept-reply escalation gap). The premise was whether an Accept reply can legally arrive with a ballot higher than the coordinator's own. It can: any recovery raises acceptors' ballots because handlePrepare assigns inst.bal = prepare.Ballot when the prepare ballot is higher (epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187), and handleAccept explicitly handles the stale case, logging 'Smaller ballot' and replying with the local inst.bal for accept.Ballot < inst.bal (epaxos/epaxos.go:993-1006). So when a slow-path Accept broadcast overlaps a concurrent recovery of the same instance, the Accept replies from the recovered acceptors carry the higher ballot and are dropped by handleAcceptReply's equality guard (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) before the (unreachable) greater-than block at epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035. The higher-ballot escalation that the parallel handlePreAcceptReply path performs (nacks++ and, for a leader, makeBallot + bcastPrepare, epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870) therefore has no counterpart on the Accept path. I am not yet forming an obligation: the remaining discriminator is whether the resulting non-completion is a defect given that executeCommands re-enqueues recovery after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, and that requires grounding the progress duty rather than inferring it from the parallel handler.

feedback.answered: Reachability of a higher-ballot AcceptReply is grounded: recovery raises an acceptor's instance ballot (handlePrepare sets inst.bal = prepare.Ballot when higher, epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187) and a stale Accept is answered with that higher local bal while only logging 'Smaller ballot' (epaxos/epaxos.go:993-1006). A slow-path Accept overlapping a concurrent recovery therefore yields Accept replies whose ballot exceeds the coordinator's lb.lastTriedBallot, and handleAcceptReply drops them at the equality guard without counting a nack or triggering makeBallot/bcastPrepare.
